verdicts.mechanism: Receiver tail-exemption timer-SACK (K_TAIL)
verdicts.claim: Tail branch 'bypasses cadence gate; does not reset cadence clock'
verdicts.corrected_value: It bypasses the cadence gate (returns before `elapsed` is computed) and leaves `last_ack_ns` and `since_last_ack` untouched — but it DOES advance the clock the cadence/quota gate actually reads. `elapsed = now − last_emit_any()` and `last_emit_any() = last_ack_ns.max(last_tail_ack_ns)`, so every tail SACK defers the next cadence-path and quota-path emission by up to one full interval. Spec §16.1:999 states the unified clock is intended, so the code is spec-conformant and the finding's parenthetical is the error.
evidence: receiver.rs:288-291 `if tail_due { self.last_tail_ack_ns = now_ns; self.burn_quota(); return self.build_ack(now_ns); }`
receiver.rs:292 `let elapsed = now_ns.saturating_sub(self.last_emit_any());`
receiver.rs:327-329 `fn last_emit_any(&self) -> u64 { self.last_ack_ns.max(self.last_tail_ack_ns) }`
specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:999 "referans = last_emit_any (tail-dahil birleşik-saat)"
verdicts.note: Also worth recording: the tail branch calls burn_quota() (receiver.rs:290), so tail emissions consume episode credit and count toward the K-4 hard invariant — consistent with §16.1:997 'her emisyon-yolu (freq/timer/tail) kredi düşürür'.
